newsitem.title: USA: Ford's new transmission to create 550 jobs.
newsitem.headline: Ford's new transmission to create 550 jobs.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said Monday about 550 new jobs will be created when it begins production of a new front-wheel-drive automatic transmission at its Van Dyke, Mich. and Sharonville, Ohio transmission plants.
Production is due to start toward the end of the decade.
Ford said about two thirds of the new jobs will be at Van Dyke and the others at Sharonville.
The new transmissions will be installed in the next generation of small cars built in Ford plants worldwide.
In the past few years Ford has revised almost its entire automatic transmission lineup.

This is the second major Ford investment at the Sharonville Plant in the past year. A new flexible automatic transmission line is currently being installed at the plant for the production of rear-wheel-drive transmissions. The $180 million line will begin operations early next year.

Ford's request for a 10-year, 75 percent abatement of personal property taxes on up to $90 million of investment at the Sharonville plant was approved by the Hamilton County, Ohio, Board of Commissioners and the Sharonville City Council in September.
The abatement does not affect prior assessments. In 1995, Ford paid more than $2.6 million in real and personal property taxes to governmental units within Hamilton County.

The Sharonville plant currently builds the E40D automatic transmission, which is installed in the best selling F-Series, the new Ford Expedition and other light trucks. About 1,900 people are employed at the plant.
